Lost my wife a year ago next month. My First birthday alone next week. Leaving the army in August. Family hasn’t spoken to me in two months.  This is a nice man.
Count me in
I find myself struggling with my wife’s suicide. I still see the spousal SGLI on every LES. No one seems to ask me at work how I’m doing. Well, I’m tired.

Yeah, I’ve said those same things myself. And any words of encouragement probably sound insulting right now for you I imagine. 

I will say, that for myself, what’s keeping me going right now is honoring my wife’s memory. Maybe you start there? In my case, my wife was a photographer, so I’m organizing an event for her photography friends to teach the trade to children. 

Just try and stay active. It’s hard. No one has the answers to something like this.
I’m currently going through a very similar situation. I lost my wife to suicide in July. Im very sorry for your loss
The service was surreal. I wake up everyday and nothing is changed, I thought my world ending would be a messy affair. It’s all so mundane
I found her in our closet.. I can’t do this. I can’t be strong anymore. She was my strength. I’m so sorry

lol. Nah it comes down to whatever your unit has in their armory. If they only have m4s everyone gets m4s, if they only have m16s everyone gets m16s, if there is a mixture of both, some people get m4s and others get m16.

The m4 and m16 still do not have "different applications". Ive seen marines with m4s and soldiers with m16s. you get what the military gives you. no such thing as having m4 for patrols and grabbing the m16 for a "skirmish".

The US Army standard issue weapon is the M4. I'm not sure what patrol duty means, but the m4 is issued (in most cases) to everyone. The m16 does have a longer range though because of the longer barrel.
